facts.value: A 9564-byte NOBITS allocation with five global objects in linked order: hsd_804D1138 size 0x10 at offset 0; hsd_804D1148 size 0x1200 at 0x10; hsd_804D2348 size 0x300 at 0x1210; hsd_804D2648 size 0x828 at 0x1510; hsd_804D2E70 size 0x824 at 0x1D38. The definition of hsd_804D2648 is a u8 backing array; the JPEG encoder overlays JpegWork, which includes a jmp_buf at offset zero and coefficient/DC work fields. It is not merely jmp_buf-sized storage.
facts.rationale: Full owned canonical/rendered EOF read and bounded card/JPEG consumers inspected. Current existing object layouts and named external relocations independently verified; compiled-evidence.json SHA-256 d11fb2e0b0328dfa0d9af2d8f97ab938ffac9c44d3ba8561225bcbc7db01e856. Do not confuse byte backing declaration with consumer overlay or comment history with a rebuilt matching experiment.

facts.value: A 32-byte NOBITS allocation containing eight global s32 objects in increasing-address order hsd_804D7980 through hsd_804D799C. The first two are declared volatile. Card consumers use these as command/queue cursors and control/status words. Both existing source and split sections are eight-byte aligned with ALLOC|WRITE flags; zero-initialized storage does not describe later reset values.

facts.value: A data-only C translation unit defining five bulk arrays and eight s32 globals, with no functions or owned header. Existing source and split objects agree on 9564-byte .bss and 32-byte .sbss layouts. Consumers reinterpret the bulk storage as card context/command queues and a JPEG encoder JpegWork overlay; canonical hsd_804D2648 remains declared u8[0x828], while the shared header exposes only a __jmp_buf view.
